newsitem.title: USA: Weyerhaeuser sees $0.12/shr charge in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Weyerhaeuser sees $0.12/shr charge in Q1.

text.p: Weyerhaeuser Co said Monday it expects to take an after-tax charge of about $25 million or 12 cents a common share against earnings in the first quarter of 1997.

The charge reflects the impact of closure, consolidation or disposition of recycling facilities, the permanent closure of its corrugated medium machine at Longview, Wash., the anticipated sale of Shemin Nurseries, a nursery business based in Danbury, Conn., and interest income from favorable federal tax decision relating to casualty losses arising from the eruption of Mount St. Helens in 1980, it said.

"Recycling remains a core business, but we must make some adjustments to our nationwide system... (requiring) us to close, consolidate or dispose of selected recycling assets," said John W. Creighton Jr., president and chief executive officer of of the company.

The corrugated medium machine at Longview is not large enough to be cost-competitive while the sale of Shemin, its the last nursery distribution operations, demonstrates the company's continuing efforts to tighten focus on its principal business segments, he said.

He also cited the previously announced agreement to sell Weyerhaeuser Mortgage Co as part of those efforts. He said sale of the mortgage unit is expected to close in the second quarter of 1997, subject to regulatory approvals and other contingencies. If the deal closes as anticipated, it will
have a "material favorable effect" on the company's operating results and cash flow in the quarter in which it closes, he said.
